import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from scipy.signal import find_peaks

def polynomial_baseline(x, y, order=5):
    # Simple polynomial fit for background subtraction
    poly = np.polyfit(x, y, order)
    return np.polyval(poly, x)

# Load the strong bg file
file_bg = files[0]
cols = file_bg["columns"]
print(f"Columns in {file_bg['filename']}: {cols}")

# Identify shift and intensity columns based on value ranges
x_col = None
y_col = None
for col in cols:
    data = file_bg["table"][col]
    if np.issubdtype(data.dtype, np.number):
        if np.mean(data) > 100 and np.std(data) > 10: # Likely intensity
            y_col = col
        elif np.min(data) < 4000 and np.max(data) > 0: # Likely Raman shift
            x_col = col

if x_col is None or y_col is None:
    # Fallback to index if naming is obscure
    x_col = cols[0]
    y_col = cols[1]

x = file_bg["table"][x_col]
y = file_bg["table"][y_col]

# Background subtraction
baseline = polynomial_baseline(x, y, order=5)
y_corrected = y - baseline

# Peak detection
peaks, _ = find_peaks(y_corrected, height=np.max(y_corrected)*0.1, distance=20)

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 8))

plt.subplot(2, 1, 1)
plt.plot(x, y, label='Raw Spectrum', color='gray')
plt.plot(x, baseline, label='Estimated Baseline', color='red', linestyle='--')
plt.title(f"Raw Spectrum and Background - {file_bg['filename']}")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)

plt.subplot(2, 1, 2)
plt.plot(x, y_corrected, label='Corrected Spectrum', color='blue')
plt.plot(x[peaks], y_corrected[peaks], "x", color='red', label='Detected Peaks')
plt.title("Restored Spectrum (Baseline Subtracted)")
plt.legend()
plt.grid(True)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()

print("Detected Peak Positions:")
for p in peaks:
    print(f"Shift: {x[p]:.2f}, Intensity: {y_corrected[p]:.2f}")
